title: The Big Bang
contents: The universe expands from an extremely hot, dense state, setting the stage for matter, galaxies, and eventually the atoms that make up every modern technology.

title: First stars ignite
contents: The first stars forge heavy elements in their cores and disperse them when they die, providing the raw materials for planets and life.

title: Earth forms
contents: Accretion of dust and rock builds planet Earth. Its crust, oceans, and atmosphere begin to form over the next hundreds of millions of years.

title: First life
contents: Simple single-celled organisms appear in the oceans. All life — and eventually all intelligence that builds technology — descends from them.

title: Great Oxidation Event
contents: Cyanobacteria flood the atmosphere with oxygen. This toxic waste product for earlier life makes aerobic energy and complex cells possible.

title: Eukaryotes appear
contents: Cells with a nucleus emerge through endosymbiosis — mitochondria were once free-living bacteria. Complex cells are the basis of all multicellular life.

title: Multicellular life diversifies
contents: Cooperation between cells allows larger, specialized organisms. Sponges and early animals appear in the oceans.

title: Cambrian Explosion
contents: An enormous burst of animal diversity: the major body plans, eyes, and skeletons that define most modern animal groups evolve in tens of millions of years.

title: Plants conquer land
contents: Moss-like plants colonize the continents, transforming rock into soil and the atmosphere, and creating the fossil fuels we burn today.

title: Tiktaalik emerges
contents: Tiktaalik is a transitional animal between a fish and a tetrapod. Its front fins show arm-like skeletal structures more akin to those of a crocodile, including a shoulder, elbow and wrist.

title: First forests
contents: The first trees grow into vast forests. Buried and compressed, this early wood becomes the coal that powers the Industrial Revolution.

title: Dinosaurs dominate
contents: Dinosaurs rise to dominate the land for 165 million years — until an asteroid impact clears the way for mammals to inherit the Earth.

title: First flowers bloom
contents: Angiosperms — flowering plants — evolve and rapidly spread, reshaping ecosystems and enabling most of modern agriculture.

title: Hominins diverge
contents: The lineage leading to humans splits from that of chimpanzees. Bipedal walking frees the hands for tool use.

title: First stone tools
contents: Flaked stone tools mark the dawn of deliberate technology — the first step on the long road to every machine we build.

title: Control of fire
contents: Early humans harness fire for warmth, light, and cooking. Cooking unlocks more energy for ever-larger brains.

title: The Agricultural Revolution
contents: Humans begin domesticating plants and animals in the Fertile Crescent. Permanent settlements and surplus food make civilization possible.

title: Writing is invented
contents: Sumerian cuneiform records trade and laws. Writing lets knowledge outlive its authors — the basis of science and every stored technology.
